info.title: Research Hub API
info.description:
The self-hosted research hub's API, for scripts, the CLI and AI agents. Neo4j holds metadata, note text and your personal layer; files are LINKS (`file_url`: Google Drive, arXiv, a publisher). Uploading a PDF sends it to the owner's Google Drive; the hub stores only the link. The library can be exported/imported as CSL JSON, and the whole graph backed up and restored as one JSON file. All private endpoints need the owner token (`Authorization: Bearer ...`) or a signed-in session. When served under a path (BASE_PATH), prefix every path.

Limits: requests are rate limited per client IP (all /api: RATE_LIMIT_PER_MIN, default 600/min; expensive endpoints such as /api/analysis, /api/audit, /api/query, /mcp, backup/restore, import/export, enrich and notes sync share HEAVY_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MIN, default 120/min; /api/login: 10 failed attempts per 10 minutes). Over the limit the answer is 429 with Retry-After. Bodies over an endpoint's size limit get 413. One analysis takes at most 200 links and 300 fields, a link field at most 100 values, and a list search at most 500 characters. In production, unexpected errors are answered "Internal error" with a request_id; the details are in the server log.

bearerAuth.description: Value of HUB_API_TOKEN on the server.

PaperItem.description: A reference-manager style item. Send a full item, or just {"DOI": "..."} and the hub looks the metadata up on Crossref. Unknown fields are ignored.

DOI.description: Used as the paper identity (doi:<lowercase>) and for duplicate detection.

tags.description: Strings or {tag}. Conventions: topic:<name>, public. A status:<value> tag is forwarded to the personal layer (not stored on the paper).

file_url.description: Optional. https link to the PDF (Google Drive share link, arXiv, a publisher). Stored as given (Drive links are normalised); nothing is downloaded.

copy_to_drive.description: With file_url: download the PDF (host must be in PDF_FETCH_ALLOWED_HOSTS, default arxiv.org, export.arxiv.org, discovery.ucl.ac.uk) and upload it to the owner's Google Drive. Falls back to keeping the original link and reports file_error.

Artifact.description: Fields of any type in schema/schema.json other than papers (method, use_case, case_study, note, project). Collections (method, use_case, case_study) also accept their own schema fields, e.g. kind, purpose, procedure (method), goal, scenario, status (use_case), case_type, sources, outcomes (case_study): see GET /api/schema and schema/schema.json. Relation fields take artifact keys (e.g. "doi:10.1/x", "method:tdd").

fields.description: Fields from schema/schema.json (GET /api/schema). Link fields take names (resolved to vocabulary nodes) or keys; objects and lists of objects as JSON. Unknown fields are kept; a reading status is set with /api/personal.

slug.description: Optional key slug (default: from the title)

copy_to_drive.description: Papers: copy the PDF to Drive

fields.description: Every schema field; link fields as {key, name} (key null for text written by older versions)

extra.description: Fields the schema does not know, kept as sent

rel.description: A relation_types name (ADDRESSES) or its field name (addresses)

confidence.description: one level, or per field (default medium)

empty_core_standard.description: fields of the requested tier still empty

flagged.description: ungrounded findings and interpretive links without a location

post.summary: Save Claude's analysis of an item in one call (no approval step)
post.description: Finds the item (key, or a paper by doi or url, or a new method/use case/case study by fields.title) or creates it. For papers, source facts come from Crossref and OpenAlex server-side (authors as Person nodes, venue as a Venue node, citation count, open access, language). Claude's fields are saved with provenance (by=claude, model, confidence, status=auto) and fill empty fields only: the owner's values and reviewed values are never overwritten, and force replaces only Claude's own. Links: vocabulary targets by name, items by key or exact title (never created from a name); interpretive links need evidence. Key findings without a location are saved but flagged ungrounded.
